events.title: First working Lisp interpreter
events.summary: By May 1959, John McCarthy's Lisp interpreter at [MIT] was working well enough for real research on the [IBM] 704.
events.about: Lisp treated programs as data you could manipulate — built for AI and symbolic work like theorem proving and language experiments. It later influenced Emacs, CAD tools, and languages from Python to Clojure.

narrative.whyChosen: Lisp introduced a new way to write programs as nested lists — ideas that later shaped AI tools, text editors, and [functional programming].
narrative.whyImportant: It proved that treating code like data could power real research tools, not just theory.
narrative.problemSolved: Researchers working on reasoning and AI needed a language for symbols and logic, not just the number-crunching style of FORTRAN.
